title: What Queue really does, and where your picture went

questions.q: You press Queue twice with nothing changed, and SaveImage is in the graph. How many new files appear?
options: Two, unless the seed is fixed
questions.why: The second run finds every result in the cache, including SaveImage's. In our run the output folder held one file and the second history entry repeated the first record.

questions.q: Where does PreviewImage write its file?
options: Into the temp folder, with the record type temp
Nowhere, it stays in the browser
questions.answer: Into the temp folder, with the record type temp
questions.why: PreviewImage is a SaveImage that points at the temp directory. The page then fetches it with /view and type=temp.

questions.q: The output folder holds ComfyUI_00001_, 00002_ and 00009_. What is the next number?
questions.why: get_save_image_path takes the largest number it finds and adds one. Gaps are never filled.

questions.q: You restart the server. What survives?
options: The saved files survive and the history list does not
Both the files and the history
The history and not the files
questions.answer: The saved files survive and the history list does not
questions.why: History is a dictionary in memory. Files in the output folder are ordinary files on disk.

questions.q: A script posts a prompt with filename_prefix set to %date:yyyy-MM-dd%/x. What folder does it get?
options: A folder named with today's date
questions.why: The editor expands %date:...% before sending. The server only knows %year%, %month%, %day%, %hour%, %minute%, %second%, %width% and %height%. A run of the real function confirmed it.
